signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5923 continues to lead G10 performance, buoyed by the RBNZ's active hiking cycle and a 125bp carry advantage over the USD. The pair is currently testing levels above its SMA200 at 0.5835, with the G10 scorecard confirming a strong bilateral theme as NZD outperforms the lagging USD by a 1.421% spread. While the RBNZ holds a negative real rate of -1.56% due to high inflation expectations, the market remains focused on nominal policy divergence as the 2 Sep meeting approaches. Speculative positioning in NZD remains at a 52-week extreme short (pctl 2, z -2.00), creating an asymmetric short-squeeze environment as data continues to beat expectations (ESI +7.9). A sustained break above the SMA20/50/200 cluster confirms the bullish momentum against a crowded spec short. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD, asymmetric squeeze setup supported by G10 outperformance. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike priced. Risk: RBNZ pauses or signals a dovish shift, allowing the crowded spec short to reassert control.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + Positioning
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.91, holding below the 160.00 psychological barrier and its SMA20/50 cluster (160.49/161.10). A 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential provides a structural bid, yet the options market signals deep caution with a strong 25d risk reversal put skew of -2.08. This suggests institutional desks are paying a premium for downside protection despite the significant carry advantage. Leveraged funds have reduced JPY net shorts by +45k over the last four weeks, though the net position remains short at -59,526. The combination of falling spot, negative VRP (-1.4%), and a shifting correlation with VIX (z=+1.46σ) indicates the JPY is no longer responding to traditional safe-haven triggers but is instead sensitive to policy repricing. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY, carry support offset by aggressive downside options hedging. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 60% hike priced) — hike bias. Risk: BoJ holds rates and hawkish bets recede, allowing carry-seekers to re-engage toward 160.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7125 maintains a bullish posture, supported by a 60bp carry advantage over the Fed and a restrictive real rate of +0.55%. Technical support is firm at the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7025/0.6994/0.6939), though positioning data warns of a crowded long trade. Leveraged funds are net long +45,727, while retail sentiment has reached an 81% short extreme, creating a clear institutional-vs-retail divergence. While retail is fading the trend, the moderate negative ESI (-12.7) suggests Australian macro data is not yet fully justifying the extent of the recent move. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail capitulation risk supports further upside toward 0.7200. Catalyst: next high-impact US macro release. Risk: 4W positioning adds stall, signaling late-cycle exhaustion in the spec long trade.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + Technicals
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3563 is trading above all major moving averages, with the SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3428/1.3374/1.3416) acting as a formidable support floor. The options market is pricing in significant risk with an IV of 11.0% against an HV30 of 6.1%, resulting in a massive +4.9% Vol Risk Premium. This elevated hedging demand suggests traders are bracing for a volatility spike despite the pair's steady climb. Speculative positioning is approaching 52-week extremes (pctl 90, z +1.23) as the carry differential vs the USD has neutralized at 0bp. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, high vol premium warrants caution on fresh long entries. Catalyst: UK inflation data next week. Risk: UK CPI misses expectations, triggering an unwind of the 90th-percentile spec long position.
